claims.quote: In the testis, LH binds to LH receptors on Leydig cells and stimulates the release of testosterone.

source.section: 27.1 Anatomy and Physiology of the Testicular Reproductive System
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: It produces testosterone, an androgen and steroid hormone.
claims.quote: Testosterone, an androgen, is a steroid hormone produced by Leydig cells.

source.section: 27.1 Anatomy and Physiology of the Testicular Reproductive System
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Sitting in the interstitial area between the seminiferous tubules of the testis, it secretes testosterone.
claims.quote: A Leydig cell is a testosterone-secreting cell in the interstitial area, between the seminiferous tubules, in the testis.

claims.value: Receptors on the cell bind luteinizing hormone (LH), which steps up its testosterone production.
claims.quote: LH binds to receptors on Leydig cells in the testes and upregulates the production of testosterone.

source.section: 27.1 Anatomy and Physiology of the Testicular Reproductive System
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: When stimulated by LH, it makes testosterone and releases it both into the testes and into the blood.
claims.quote: LH also enters the testes and stimulates the interstitial cells of Leydig to make and release testosterone into the testes and the blood.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: In the embryonic testis, the testosterone it makes drives development of the male sexual organs.
claims.quote: Testosterone produced by Leydig cells in the embryonic testis stimulates the development of male sexual organs.

source.section: 27.3 Development of the Male and Female Reproductive Systems
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: The testosterone it produces is also responsible for male secondary sexual characteristics.
claims.quote: The Leydig cells produce testosterone, which also is responsible for the secondary sexual characteristics of males.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.
